featured_reviews.review_text:
A visit to the Jogeshwari Caves offers a fascinating glimpse into Mumbai's deep historical roots, dating all the way back to 560 CE. If you are a history or archaeology enthusiast, set aside 1–2 hours to explore this ancient site.
Key Highlights & What to Expect
Ancient Heritage: The sheer age of these caves is awe-inspiring. They hold immense historical value as one of the oldest surviving rock-cut Hindu temple caves in the city.

featured_reviews.name: Veludharan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jogeshwari Caves hewed during 6th century CE, is one of the finest specimen of Brahmanical rock-cut architecture and bears similarity with Elephanta (Cave no.1) and Dhumar lena (Cave no. 29) at Ellora. On plan, it consists of agra mandapa, mukha mandapa and garbhagriha. Vakataka and later Vakataka, influence can clearly be noticed in its architectural planning and sculptural execution. Some scholars believe that the caves were excavated under the patronage of Maurya of Konkan, Kalachuri (Traikutakas). Jogeshwari cave is adorned with a few beautiful sculptural representations of Lakulisa. Kalyansundarmurti, Shiv Parvati playing dyuta, Natraja, Ravananugraha, Makartornas, ayudhprushas, Dwarapalas etc.
It was declared as a protected monument of national importance by the Archaeological Survey of India, vide gazette notification no. 2704A, dated 26.05. 1009

featured_reviews.name: Vaibhav Gajur
featured_reviews.review_text:
A visit to the Jogeshwari Caves offers a fascinating glimpse into Mumbai's deep historical roots, dating all the way back to 560 CE. If you are a history or archaeology enthusiast, set aside 1–2 hours to explore this ancient site.
Key Highlights & What to Expect
Ancient Heritage: The sheer age of these caves is awe-inspiring. They hold immense historical value as one of the oldest surviving rock-cut Hindu temple caves in the city.
Weathered Carvings: Be prepared that many of the old carvings are heavily weathered. While their original splendor may be diminished, they still tell a story of a distant past.
Unique Temple Setup: The main sanctum is a must-see. The temple dedicated to Goddess Jogeshwari Mata is located in the basement. You will also find shrines for Lord Shiva in one corner and a more hidden shrine for Lord Hanuman in another.
East Gate Temple: If you enter or exit via the East Gate, you'll find a separate temple dedicated to Lord Ganesh.
Multiple Entrances: The caves are accessible via two main entrances, one on the East and one on the West.
📸 Pro-Tip: The Hidden Viewpoint
After exploring the basement shrine, make sure to ask a local for the way to the top of the caves. The journey offers a reward: a good panoramic view of the entire structure and surrounding area.
🕉️ Other Shrines Nearby
The complex holds several other important deities worth visiting:
There is a second dedicated temple to Lord Hanuman (ask a local for directions, as it might be slightly hidden).
Look for a temple housing Kal Bhairav and other deities on the other side of the complex.
⏱️ Essential Visiting Hours
Please note the specific timings for your visit:
The temple is closed during the afternoon.
It reopens in the evening at 4 PM.
Recommendation: Visit in the early morning or late evening to experience the temple and avoid the mid-day closure.
Overall: Jogeshwari Caves is a unique, spiritual, and historical experience. While the carvings are worn, the atmosphere and the ancient rock-cut architecture make this a worthwhile stop for anyone interested in Mumbai's pre-medieval history.

featured_reviews.name: Suresh Isave
featured_reviews.review_text: The Jogeshwari Caves feature beautiful carvings, though some aspects appear unfinished. Parking is also an issue, as none is available close by. Entry is free.

featured_reviews.name: Kunal Singh
featured_reviews.review_text: The Jogeshwari Caves act as a haunting reminder of Mumbai's deep ancient roots, representing some of the earliest and most significant Hindu and Buddhist rock-cut architecture in the region. Stepping inside, one can still sense the majesty of the past through the massive pillars and the lingering spiritual aura of the central Shiva shrine. However, the site is in a heartbreaking state of decay, suffocated by encroaching slums and plagued by sewage seepage and piled-up debris that obscure its historical value. It is a heritage monument that is desperately crying out for comprehensive restoration and protection; without immediate intervention to clear the surroundings and preserve the crumbling rockwork, this archaeological treasure risks being lost entirely to urban neglect.

featured_reviews.name: Amit Gurav
featured_reviews.review_text:
The caves are located just off the Western Express Highway and are surrounded by heavy encroachments. Access is through a long flight of stairs that leads into the main hall of the cavern. Unfortunately, the site is in very poor condition—extremely unhygienic, poorly maintained, and the area smells terrible.

I would strongly advise against making a special trip, as you are likely to feel disappointed and even upset by the neglect and lack of care shown by the authorities and local people. The site remains open at all times with no entry gate or time restrictions, which further contributes to its deteriorated state.

featured_reviews.name: RuSo
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited the Jogeshwari Caves and it was a surprisingly powerful experience. One of the oldest rock-cut cave temples in India, the place has a raw, ancient energy that you can actually feel as you walk inside. The carvings dedicated to Lord Shiva, especially forms like Nataraja, are beautiful and carry a quiet intensity.

The caves are not very well maintained compared to places like Elephanta Caves, and there can be waterlogging and a bit of mess around, but that also adds to the untouched, authentic feel of the site.

If you enjoy history, architecture, or just want a peaceful spot away from the usual crowds, this place is worth a visit. A hidden gem in Mumbai that deserves more care and attention.

Shivaji Park is not just a ground — it’s an emotion for every cricket lover. If you really want to watch future superstars of Indian cricket in the making, this is the place to be. On the red soil of this historic ground, you’ll see young kids practicing with full dedication, sweating it out under the sharp Mumbai sun, chasing their dreams with bat and ball in hand.
There’s something special about standing there and watching them play. The sound of leather hitting the bat, coaches shouting instructions, and parents cheering from the side — it all feels raw and real. Many legends, including Sachin Tendulkar, began their journey here, which makes the atmosphere even more inspiring.
The park is huge, so even if you're not into cricket, it’s a perfect place for a peaceful walk or to just sit and relax. In the evening, the cool breeze and open space make it ideal for clearing your mind after a long day.
And of course, no visit is complete without trying the famous vada pav near Shivaji Park. The street food around the area is amazing — simple, authentic, and full of Mumbai flavor. Grabbing a hot vada pav after watching an intense practice session just feels right.

Similar but bigger in size to Azad Maidan and August Kranti Maidan (formerly Gowalia Tank Grounds), it is of historical and cultural value because of the political and social gatherings it has witnessed, both in pre- and post-independence Mumbai. The 113,000 square metres (28 acres) of open space is renowned as having been a cradle of the game of cricket in India.

featured_reviews.name: Ayaj Deshmukh
featured_reviews.review_text:
🌿 A Majestic Experience at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Park
🏞️ Pride of Dadar, Mumbai | A Historic Ground of Courage & Culture 👑🇮🇳
Visiting Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Park in Dadar, Mumbai, was a truly memorable, emotional, and inspiring experience for me 💚. This park is not just an open ground—it is a historical landmark that carries the spirit of Maharashtra’s pride, unity, and rich legacy 🌟. The moment I stepped onto this vast green land, I felt a deep sense of respect and belonging 🙏.
The park is named after Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, the great Maratha warrior king who symbolizes bravery, good governance, and Swarajya 👑⚔️. Standing here, I could feel the echoes of history in the air. This ground has witnessed many historic political movements, social gatherings, freedom-related events, and public speeches that shaped modern Maharashtra 🇮🇳📜. Knowing this made my visit even more meaningful and powerful.
As I walked through the park, I noticed people of all ages—children playing, elders walking peacefully, students practicing sports, and groups doing yoga 🏃‍♂️🧘‍♀️. The park beautifully balances history and daily life, showing how the past and present coexist harmoniously 🌸. The lush greenery and open space provide a refreshing escape from the busy city life of Mumbai 🌳🌬️.
One of the most emotional aspects of my visit was realizing that this very ground has been a platform for voices demanding justice, equality, and rights ✊. Many great leaders have addressed the nation from here, making it a silent witness to India’s democratic journey 🗣️📢. Being present at such a historically significant place filled me with pride and responsibility as a citizen 🤍.
The surrounding area reflects Mumbai’s cultural richness, with nearby temples, roads filled with local life, and a strong sense of Maharashtrian identity 🎭🪔. The park stands as a reminder that public spaces can unite people beyond caste, religion, and background, just like the ideals of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj himself 🤝.
As the evening breeze touched my face and the sky slowly changed colors 🌅, I felt calm yet energized. This place doesn’t just relax the body—it awakens the soul. It teaches us discipline, unity, and respect for our roots 🌱.
In conclusion, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Park is more than a park—it is a living chapter of Indian history 🏞️📖. Every visit deepens respect for our heritage and inspires us to live with courage, integrity, and love for the nation 🚩✨.

featured_reviews.review_text:
There’s something about Dadar Chowpatty that just feels like home. It’s not 'fancy' like some of the other beaches, but that’s exactly why I love it.
I came here last Tuesday after a really long day at work, and honestly, it was exactly what I needed. I just sat on the sand for an hour, watched the waves, and looked at the Sea Link glowing in the distance. It’s one of those rare places in Mumbai where you can actually hear your own thoughts.
I ended up chatting with an old uncle who’s been coming here for 30 years, and he told me the beach has its own rhythm. You see families laughing, couples holding hands, and students stressed about exams—all just co-existing.
A few 'human' tips if you go:
• The Chana Chor Garam: Get a cone from the guy near the entrance. It’s the perfect salty snack for a walk.
• The Rocks: Be careful if you sit on the tetrapods! They’re great for photos, but they can be slippery.
• The Timing: Go right when the sun is dipping. The sky turns this incredible shade of pink and orange that no camera can really catch.
If you’re feeling a bit overwhelmed by the city pace, come here. Buy a kulfi, kick off your shoes, and just exist for a bit. It’s good for the soul. ❤️

featured_reviews.review_text:
While Mumbai is famous for its coastal charm, Dadar Chowpatty is a stark reminder of the city's struggle with pollution and overcrowding. If you are expecting a relaxing beach day, you will likely leave disappointed.
​The Reality of the Shoreline
​The most immediate and overwhelming issue is the lack of cleanliness. The sand is often covered in a thick layer of plastic waste, debris, and tidal filth. Walking barefoot is out of the question, and the general state of the beach makes it feel more like a landfill than a recreational escape.
​A Sensory Overload (For the Wrong Reasons)
​The Odor: Due to the accumulation of waste and the proximity to drainage outlets, the air often carries a strong, unpleasant smell that makes it difficult to sit and enjoy the breeze for long.
​Overcrowding: Particularly on weekends, the narrow strip of usable sand becomes incredibly cramped. It lacks the organized chaos of Juhu or the spaciousness of Girgaon, feeling instead cluttered and chaotic.
​Water Quality: The water here is visibly polluted and murky. It is definitely not a place where you would want to dip your feet, let alone swim.
​The Only Silver Lining
​The only saving grace of this location is the view of the Bandra-Worli Sea Link in the distance. However, you are much better off enjoying that view from the nearby Dadar Sea View Deck, which allows you to appreciate the skyline without having to step into the grime of the beach itself.
​Verdict: Avoid Dadar Chowpatty if you are looking for a "beach experience." It is poorly maintained and visually unappealing. Unless you are just passing through to get to the viewing deck, your time is better spent at almost any other promenade in the city.

featured_reviews.name: Travelling Doctor
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you have just finished a visit to the nearby Dadar Sea View Deck or are trying to escape the grime of Dadar Chowpatty, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Park is the perfect palate cleanser. It is not just a park; it is the "beating heart" of Mumbai’s cultural and sporting life.
The "Cradle of Champions"
The energy here is infectious. Known globally as the nursery of Indian cricket, you can watch dozens of local matches and net practices happening simultaneously. This is the very ground where legends like Sachin Tendulkar and Sunil Gavaskar honed their skills. Even if you aren't a sports fan, sitting on the katta  and watching the sunset while the sound of leather hitting willow echoes across the 28-acre expanse is a quintessential Mumbai experience.
Why It’s Great for Adults & Walkers
The Walking Circuit: The park features a well-paved outer promenade and an inner jogging track (approx. 1.2 km). It is arguably the best place in Dadar for a long, uninterrupted walk or jog, shaded by massive, ancient rain trees.
The "Katta" Culture: The perimeter wall serves as a massive, communal bench. It’s a wonderful spot to sit, enjoy the sea breeze, and people-watch. You’ll see everyone from senior citizens discussing politics at the "Nana-Nani Park" to young students and professionals unwinding after work.
Heritage & Atmosphere: The area surrounding the park is one of Mumbai’s most charming residential neighborhoods. The architecture is a mix of Art Deco and traditional Maharashtrian styles, giving the whole place a dignified, "old-world" soul that you won't find in the newer parts of the city.
A Culinary Finish
The periphery of the park is a goldmine for authentic Maharashtrian street food. After your walk, you can grab some of the city's best Vada Pav, Sabudana Vada, or a refreshing glass of Piyush from iconic local stalls like Prakash Shakahari Upahaar Kendra or Aaswad, which are just a short walk away.
Verdict: While the nearby beach may be disappointing, Shivaji Park is pristine, vibrant, and full of life. It is the perfect spot for a morning workout, a peaceful evening stroll, or simply soaking in the history of Mumbai.

I recently visited Shivaji Park Point in Dadar, Mumbai, and I must say, it was an absolute delight. Nestled amidst the bustling city, this place offered a refreshing escape from the chaos, providing a serene oasis for relaxation and recreation.

The park's lush greenery and well-maintained landscapes create a picturesque setting, perfect for a leisurely stroll or a picnic with friends and family. The wide pathways and ample seating areas ensure that visitors can comfortably explore the park and find their own peaceful spot.

The highlight of Shivaji Park Point is the stunning view it offers. Located at an elevated position, it provides a panoramic vista of the surrounding cityscape and the Arabian Sea. The breathtaking sunset view from here is truly mesmerizing and not to be missed.

The park also boasts excellent amenities. Clean restrooms, well-equipped play areas for children, and well-maintained sports facilities make it an ideal spot for outdoor activities. I noticed people engaged in various sports like cricket, football, and yoga, making the park vibrant and lively.

Furthermore, the park's proximity to various eateries and cafes adds to its appeal. After a leisurely walk, I enjoyed some delicious snacks and beverages at the nearby food stalls, making my visit even more enjoyable.

Overall, Shivaji Park Point in Dadar is a hidden gem that offers a tranquil escape from the city's hustle and bustle. Whether you're looking for a peaceful retreat or a fun-filled day out, this park has it all. I highly recommend visiting and experiencing the beauty and tranquility it has to offer.

One practical advantage is that it sits under the bridge stretch, so a good part of the area gets natural shade, which makes it more comfortable during the daytime compared to fully open gardens. It’s not a huge or heavily developed space, but it does its job well as a simple neighborhood spot for light activity and a short outdoor break.

featured_reviews.name: Careena Alvarez
featured_reviews.review_text: Great park to sit and chill out. There are park benches at regular intervals and on some days a cool breeze also helps make the place quite appealing to hang out at. Not a very quiet place in the sense that it's right in the middle of two very busy streets so if you need a quiet space, maybe some other park would fit the bill, but not this one. There will be a constant traffic sound around here.

featured_reviews.name: Chinmay Jaiswal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Matunga east is such a place to come and prosper peace, specially delta around King's Circle. Kudos to Municipal Corporation for such idea, design and facility, haven't seen anything like this before. You can come here and find peace amongst chaos of Mumbai Life.
Morning walk is bliss if you are around this area, also in evening the lights are so aesthetic and breathtaking.
Worth investing time at this place.

featured_reviews.name: Vikram Parikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
It's a superb park with walking lanes for jogging or running or just strolling. There is garden, slides & stuff, even benches.
There is a circular park in between and on both sides perpendicular there is long walking lane below bridge. Very calm & cozy environment.

featured_reviews.name: Austin Fernandes
featured_reviews.review_text: Beautiful garden under a flyover. The place is clean and well maintained. The pillars of the flyover have some amazing art on them. A nice place to relax for a while in the Matunga area.

featured_reviews.name: Yohann Setna
featured_reviews.review_text:
I love this place. I walk here 6 times a week, in the mornings. It's been a critical part of my weight loss programme, and I am very grateful to the people who have created this excellent facility. However, there is one major down-side. In the monsoons, it's un-usable. When the mosaic tile flooring gets even a little bit wet, it's like walking on ice.

There has also been another recent issue. Last Saturday I saw a couple of workers rip up the floor tiles at the two road crossing areas. It took them one hour to rip up the tiles. Now, 1 week later, the piles of broken tiles are still lying exactly where they were dumped on day 1. Not a single bit of work has been done since then. Why is this?

I see a stack of new floor tiles lying at one end of the area, but they are just lying there.

featured_reviews.name: Soumyajit Bose
featured_reviews.review_text: It is a curated garden under the flyover. Beautiful and well-maintained. Nearby places under this flyover is also similarly used as citizens' walking and exercise zone. This is a good initiative. However some more gardening, perhaps vertical garden, will enhance the oxygen level and aesthetics of this place. A clean and hygienic public restroom is very much required here.

featured_reviews.name: KAVYA Shukla
featured_reviews.review_text: Very good path for walking. Benches are most of the time occupied by college students. Also alot of and by that I mean ALOT OF groups of college students shoot  reels with big speakers and it is annoying as they block the way. Place was very clean and dustbin was provided and reasonable distants.

name: Mumbai Life and Spice Tours
description:
Mumbai Life and Spice Tours is led by founder Mr. Oves, a passionate local storyteller dedicated to sharing the true spirit of Mumbai. Our team of experienced local guides brings the city to life through its history, architecture, neighborhoods, food culture, and everyday rhythms.

We offer carefully curated guided tours focused on authentic experiences and cultural insights. From heritage walks and city sightseeing to food-focused journeys, each tour is thoughtfully designed to showcase Mumbai beyond the usual tourist routes.

With a strong focus on safety, comfort, and personalized service, we ensure every guest enjoys a memorable and enriching experience while discovering Mumbai as a living story.

featured_reviews.name: Janice Eyers
featured_reviews.review_text: We first used Oves as a guide in 2019. We have used him several times since when visiting Mumbai, most recently January 2026. As regular visitors to Mumbai, for no other reason than that we love it, we now like to see places that are off the tourist track and more individualistic. Oves is a born and bred Mumbaiker who does us proud by taking us around the city and showing us many different aspects of life in Mumbai. We've never tired of Oves guiding skills. Be it the tourist areas, Dharavi slum tour and some of the more offbeat areas of the city. We like walking, using local transport especially the new Metro system and local trains if necessary and Oves is very accommodating to our requests. I have recommended Oves to friends over the years and they have been very happy. I would highly recommend him if you are looking for a guided tour in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Caro Lef
featured_reviews.review_text:
We did a tour of the highlights of South mumbai.  Our tour guide Armaan was lovely and very knowledgeable.  He was also considerate of my partners disability which made our stops slow and sometimes not as far as would have been usual.  Our driver Shamser was a good driver, stopping close to sights for us.

I also did a fabulous workshop learning about Indian fabrics and block printing.  I printed a lovely bag and enjoyed it immensely.

featured_reviews.name: Brian Witte
featured_reviews.review_text:
We took two tours with Mumbai Magic - Historic Fort District and Sanjay Gandhi National Park / Kanheri Caves.

Both trips were wonderful. We learned a lot about the architecture and history of old Bombay on the first tour. Our guide, Ms. Pankaja, waited almost an hour when our taxi became lost. We still had a very good tour.

Our guide for the National Park trip had a master's degree in botany. He knew so much and was a very good teacher. Best day of my trip so far.

featured_reviews.name: Donna Lar
featured_reviews.review_text: Had a great visit to mumbia, saw lots of sites at our own pace. Pan the tour guide was very knowledgeable.  We recommend the Bollywood dance lessons, they’re great fun.

featured_reviews.name: Chris-Ann Venugopal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our tour was arranged by the concierge at Four Seasons Hotel.

We did all day tour of Mumbai one day and half day tour of Bandra another day.  Our guide was Umar on both days.  He was very friendly, knowledgeable and had great insight into all of the different places.  We saw parts of Mumbai tourist don't usually have access to see.  Very realistic portrayal of Mumbai and the surrounding areas.  He was willing to change plans as requested by us.  We saw sites, enjoyed street food that was safe and came away with a greater understanding and appreciation of the people of Mumbai.

We would highly recommend Mumbai magic tours.

featured_reviews.name: Jean Oliver
featured_reviews.review_text: We toured Mumbai today with a driver and tour guide, arranged by Mumbai Magic tours. Both driver and guide were excellent. We had only a short time in the city and wanted to see and learn as much as possible. We crammed a lot into the day from icons such as the India Gate to billion pound houses. The driver negotiated the daunting traffic with skill and care for his passengers and there appeared to be little the guide did not know. She was very professional but friendly with a great sense of humour. All the arrangements made on line worked and we were well looked after. I would not hesitate to recommend them.

featured_reviews.name: Jackie Geale
featured_reviews.review_text: We booked this Dhavari tour through Mumbai Magic after a fantastic Mumbai Local tour we had with them yesterday.  Abir, our lovely local guide, met us on time and showed us around the area where he grew up. Although he was only 20 years old, his knowledge of the area was excellent. He could answer any questions we asked and he gave us such a great insight as to how this ‘city in a city’ operates and works so well. We certainly came away with a different opinion of the area. It was a fantastic tour and we can highly recommend Mumbai Magic.

featured_reviews.name: Beth Czechanski
featured_reviews.review_text: High quality experience from booking all the way through to the tour.  Even though we booked a bit last minute, the Mumbai Magic team was super accommodating, helping us customize the perfect tour. We spent an amazing day touring Mumbai with our knowledgeable guide, Sudha, and It was entertaining and educational.  I would highly recommend any of the offerings from Mumbai Magic!

featured_reviews.name: George Jose
featured_reviews.review_text: We took the Heritage walk tour through Mumbai Magic Tours and we had a very good experience. Tour guide was very knowledgeable, friendly, patient and her language was really good too. She took time explaining each heritage site, went over some history and patiently answered all our questions. Her voice was very soft so we had to listen very carefully to hear her though. Overall, I recommend this company for this tour!
